title: Imperative and Basic Two-Way Prepositions
summary: Giving instructions and using an/auf/in in simple directional contexts.
whyItMatters: Imperatives make event instructions direct and efficient. Basic two-way prepositions add the crucial distinction between putting or moving something somewhere and describing where it already is.

mentalModel.title: Imperative starts with action
mentalModel.content: The action verb leads; the subject is usually omitted with 'du' and 'ihr' but included after the verb with formal 'Sie'.

mentalModel.title: Movement asks wohin
mentalModel.content: Use accusative after an, auf, or in when something moves to a destination.

mentalModel.title: Location asks wo
mentalModel.content: Use dative after the same prepositions when something is already located there.

ruleBlocks.title: Form the du imperative from the verb stem
ruleBlocks.content: Usually remove '-st' and the subject: 'Du kommst' becomes 'Komm!' and 'Du nimmst' becomes 'Nimm!'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use familiar plural and formal forms
ruleBlocks.content: The 'ihr' imperative matches the present form without 'ihr': 'Kommt!' Formal commands use infinitive plus 'Sie': 'Kommen Sie!'

ruleBlocks.title: Add nicht or kein for prohibitions
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Kommt nicht zu spät' or 'Bringt keine Getränke mit'.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose case from movement or location
ruleBlocks.content: Use accusative for destination ('auf den Tisch') and dative for location ('auf dem Tisch').

tables.title: Direction and Location
rows: Stell die Gläser auf den Tisch.
Die Gläser stehen auf dem Tisch.
Die Gäste sind in dem Zimmer.
Häng das Bild an die Wand.
Das Bild hängt an der Wand.

sentenceStructure: The imperative verb normally occupies first position.
The preposition's case follows meaning: destination versus location.

concepts: distinguish basic destination and location phrases
combine commands with pronouns and particles
control spatial case in complex descriptions

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies event setup and rule contexts for imperatives and placement phrases.
Celebration exchanges include short invitations and hospitable instructions such as 'Komm rein' and 'Setzen Sie sich'.

examples.de: Komm bitte um sechs Uhr und bring deine Schwester mit.
examples.en: Please come at six and bring your sister.

examples.de: Stellt die Geschenke auf den Tisch.
examples.en: Put the gifts on the table.

examples.de: Kommen Sie bitte herein und nehmen Sie Platz.
examples.en: Please come in and take a seat.
The drinks are in the refrigerator.

examples.de: Häng die Dekoration an die Wand; das Bild hängt schon an der Wand.
examples.en: Hang the decoration on the wall; the picture is already hanging on the wall.

commonMistakes.reason: The subject is normally omitted in the 'du' imperative.

commonMistakes.wrong: Stell die Gläser auf dem Tisch.
commonMistakes.correct: Stell die Gläser auf den Tisch.
commonMistakes.reason: Movement to a destination requires accusative.

specialCases: Some 'du' imperatives change the stem vowel: 'nehmen' becomes 'Nimm!'.
The distinction is semantic, not simply based on the verb: movement within a location can still answer 'wo'.
Contractions include 'ins' for 'in das' and 'im' for 'in dem'.
tips: Convert present-tense forms into all three imperative registers.
Ask 'wo' or 'wohin' before choosing the case.
Practice each location as a movement/location pair.
